answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring each new agent to lock a deposit and earn trust through randomized, cross-agent tasks. A rotating pulse of challenges links an identity to consistent behavior: a sybil cluster that fabricates endorsements eventually contradicts itself, while honest agents can expose the mismatch and trigger slashing. The attacker must fund every fake, wait through a trust spiral, and risk losing its stake when a falcon auditor catches collusion.
